answer: Every claim climbs the pigment of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the spiral re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. The design leans on staked peer review with spot checks, split across independent auditors, the unit of trust is a task, not an address. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The basalt of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
